clue.text: Selecting players for hurling

definitions.meaning: choosing the actors for a play or film
throwing, as an angler throws a line

explanation.surface: A coach picks the team for a game of hurling, the Irish stick-and-ball sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurling' looks like the Irish field game; here it simply means throwing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: choosing actors for roles, and flinging something, as with a fishing line.

clue.text: Groom and lovely female going to marry

parts.note: to groom hair is to comb it

indicators.note: going means that letter leaves the word

parts.note: fine means lovely, as in fine weather

explanation.surface: A bridegroom and his beautiful bride about to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' and 'marry' paint a wedding; 'Groom' is a verb meaning tidy hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To join or unite two things, just as a wedding unites two people.

clue.text: Slight wound is no handicap

definitions.meaning: a shallow cut or graze on the skin
a golfer playing off zero handicap is a ... player

explanation.surface: A minor injury does not hold you back.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, a 'scratch' player has a handicap of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A light graze on the skin, and the golfing term for a player with zero handicap.

clue.text: Here in Paris, Queen is more aloof

parts.note: ici is French for here
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: On a visit to Paris, the monarch is rather standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: Colder in manner; an icy person is distant and unfriendly.

clue.text: Diver's shame, eating most of fruit

definitions.note: read as 'Diver is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: eating means the word for shame takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: guilt is a sense of shame

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter

parts.note: a lemon is a fruit

explanation.surface: A scuba diver's embarrassment at eating nearly all the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' suggests a swimmer; it is a seabird that dives for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A black and white seabird of the auk family that plunges underwater after fish.

clue.text: Mum's vehicle about to start — will it run?

parts.note: MA is mum, so mum's is MA'S
a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: to start asks for only the opening letter of the word about

explanation.surface: Mum's car is about to set off: will it go?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is not C or RE here; 'to start' takes only its first letter, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye make-up notoriously streaks down the cheeks when tears or rain make it run.

clue.text: Instant tea and dark brown coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Choosing between instant tea and a strong coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' reads as instant coffee; it is a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine coffee named after a Yemeni port, also the name of a dark brown colour.

clue.text: Good person with just the same name as writer

parts.note: ST is a saint, a good person
even so means nevertheless, just the same

explanation.surface: A virtuous person happens to share a name with an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just the same' reads as identical; it means nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, the Scottish novelist of Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: Amelia B strangely approachable

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of Amelia B appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Amelia B is oddly easy to talk to.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and good-natured, so easy for others to approach.

clue.text: Smoker's item lost around hospital

indicators.note: around means the word for lost goes round the other letter

parts.note: astray means lost

explanation.surface: A cigarette smoker's belongings went missing near the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish for cigarette ash and stubs, an object a smoker uses.

clue.text: Swallow one gin cocktail

parts.note: the house martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Knock back a single gin-based drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' reads as a verb about drinking, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic mixed drink of gin and vermouth, usually served with an olive.

clue.text: Fantastical riches: husband finds treasure

indicators.note: fantastical suggests something wildly reimagined, so the letters of riches are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband stumbles upon amazing wealth and a hoard of treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treasure' looks like a noun completing the riches story; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something dear and value it greatly; both verbs mean prizing it.

clue.text: Painter a liability? Partly, among other things

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is the artist a burden? To some extent, along with plenty else.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase used in English to mean that something is one item in a longer list.

clue.text: Glower from club user initially barred

indicators.note: the opening letter is shut out, as a club bars an unwanted person at the door

parts.note: a member is someone who belongs to and uses a club

explanation.surface: A scowl from a clubgoer who was at first refused entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' looks like a scowl; read it as 'one that glows'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dying coal in a fire keeps glowing, so it is literally something that glows.

clue.text: Old number three fouled

indicators.note: fouled means messed up, so the letters of three are jumbled

explanation.surface: A former shirt number three committed a foul in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: This vapour was a historic anaesthetic, a substance that numbs, so an old 'numb-er'.

clue.text: Rest survive communist uprising

parts.note: to remain is to survive, to last

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a communist is a Red

explanation.surface: Peace returns as people outlast a communist revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' suggests a revolt; in a down clue it turns RED upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over, the remaining part of something.

clue.text: In which all men are brothers?

definitions.text: In which all men are brothers?

parts.words: In which all men are brothers?
parts.note: the slogan of universal fraternity is taken literally: a house of monks, each called Brother

explanation.surface: Asks for the place where the ideal of human brotherhood is realised.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks live together in a religious house and address one another as Brother.

clue.text: Cuss — rains damaged flower

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener swears because the rain has spoiled a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus of daffodils and jonquils, a spring bulb in bloom.

clue.text: Two scholars placed in reform school

indicators.note: placed in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to reform is to alter
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree; two of them give MAMA

explanation.surface: A pair of academics are sent to a reformatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform school' looks like one phrase; 'reform' is the outer word and 'school' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for 'nourishing mother' names the school or college one attended.

clue.text: Tough resistance with pair in Australia

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A twosome meet stiff opposition down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and demanding, requiring great effort, like a tough climb.

clue.text: One who wrote less about truth, might we infer?

definitions.text: One who wrote less about truth, might we infer?

parts.words: One who wrote less about truth, might we infer?
parts.note: the playwright's name read playfully as 'more lie', so he wrote more lies and less truth

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a certain writer was economical with the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The French comic dramatist's name is read as 'more lie', hence less truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century French comic playwright of Tartuffe, whose name punningly suggests extra lying.

clue.text: Relative's oddly naive before church

definitions.note: read as 'Relative is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word naive

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A family member is strangely innocent in front of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Study what was formerly a bomb?

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Investigate an object that was once an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: To look closely at something and inspect it carefully, which is to scrutinise it.

clue.text: Some in Jobcentre attended to request

indicators.note: Some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people went to the job office to ask for something.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is a UK government office for job-seekers.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or plead earnestly, asking urgently for something.

clue.text: Asian city or Greek one without parking

indicators.note: without means the letter is left out

parts.note: Delphi is a Greek city, home of the oracle
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Choosing between an Asian and a Greek city, the latter having nowhere to park.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital territory of India, including New Delhi, is a major city in Asia.

clue.text: Facetious talk about right presentation prop

parts.note: flip means flippant, facetious

indicators.note: about means the word for talk goes round the other letter

parts.note: chat is talk

explanation.surface: Joking chatter about getting the right visual aid for a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pad of sheets on an easel, turned over page by page as a speaker presents.

clue.text: Father due to turn up for psychiatrist

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: to turn up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A father is expected to show up for his therapy session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' looks like arriving; it reverses DUE in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund, the Viennese founder of psychoanalysis, loosely called a psychiatrist.

clue.text: Soldiers and police surrounding king

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for police goes round the other letter

parts.note: cops are police officers
R, rex, is Latin for king

explanation.surface: Troops and officers form a protective ring around the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit or body of troops, such as an army corps.

clue.text: Not settled round greenery, second rook departs

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: departs means that letter leaves the word

parts.note: verdure is lush green vegetation
R is rook in chess notation; it is the second R of the word for greenery that goes

explanation.surface: An unpaid bill around the garden, after a second chess rook leaves the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill not yet paid after its due date is late and unsettled.

clue.text: With which court proceedings ensue?

parts.note: court proceedings suggests a lawsuit, but the court is a tennis court and a rally begins with the first hit

explanation.surface: Asks what triggers a legal case going to court.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings work: delivering a writ starts legal action, and the serve starts every tennis point.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, play on court begins with the serve; in law, delivering documents starts a case.

clue.text: Time to reflect in shed with fleece removed

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to reflect means mirrored, so the word for time is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Some time to think in the garden shed after the sheep's wool came off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep whose wool has been clipped off has been shorn, its coat cut away.

clue.text: Believe to be dodgy

explanation.surface: To think something is shady.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to think something true without proof; the adjective means doubtful or untrustworthy.
